name: Canadian LTL and truckload freight carrier
modelled_on: Mullen Group Ltd. (LTL segment, including Gardewine) and TFI International Inc. (Canadian LTL and truckload operations), from their public results; scaled to a single mid-sized carrier
summary: This is a Canadian trucking company of about 3,600 employees that moves freight for manufacturers, distributors and retailers. Its largest business is less-than-truckload (LTL) freight: it collects many small shipments from shippers with city trucks, sorts them overnight through 38 terminals and five hub cross-docks in Ontario, Quebec and western Canada, and delivers them to consignees, usually in one to four days. Company drivers and about 70 contracted owner-operators pull the linehaul trailers between terminals. A truckload division hauls full trailer loads within Canada and to and from the United States, using about 430 company drivers, 310 contracted owner-operators and brokered carriers when its own fleet is full. Customers pay per shipment or per load at negotiated rates, plus a weekly fuel surcharge and charges for extras such as detention, appointments and liftgates. The company runs its own maintenance shops, recruits and trains its drivers, and must follow federal and provincial rules on hours of service, electronic logging, vehicle inspection, dangerous goods and customs reporting. Head-office departments handle sales and pricing, customer service and claims, billing and settlements, safety, HR and IT, and the company reports to a TSX-listed transportation group that owns it.

process_map.name: Transfer freight to interline partners

process_map.name: Reweigh and inspect shipments (W&I)

process_map.name: Handle dangerous goods shipments

process_map.name: Move trailers in terminal yards

process_map.name: Review terminal performance daily

process_map.name: Plan the LTL network and service standards

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Plan peak season and storm capacity

process_map.name: Rebalance empty LTL trailers

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Manage cartage agents

process_map.description: Driver trainers run orientation, winter driving and defensive driving courses, coach drivers referred for poor safety events, and renew TDG certificates before their 36-month expiry for drivers and dock workers. Records feed audits.

evidence.note: TDG certificate expiry and record rules from Transport Canada; volumes estimated.

process_map.name: Prepare for regulator facility audits
process_map.description: When a provincial regulator schedules a facility audit, compliance staff pull samples of driver files, hours-of-service records, maintenance records and inspection certificates and fix gaps. A failed audit leads to a conditional safety rating and closer monitoring.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Monitor and coach driver safety performance
process_map.description: Safety managers review telematics alerts, log violations, inspections and collisions by driver, decide on coaching, retraining or discipline, and report trends to leadership. Inconsistent follow-up weakens both safety and union relations.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Manage workplace health and safety
process_map.description: OHS specialists investigate dock and shop injuries, file workers' compensation reports, run joint health and safety committees and arrange modified duties. Forklift strikes and manual handling injuries are the common cases.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Prevent and respond to cargo theft
process_map.description: The security coordinator investigates cargo thefts, trailer break-ins and seal tampering with police and insurers, and maintains trusted-trader security programs needed for fast border clearance. Theft of loaded trailers in the Greater Toronto Area is a recurring risk.
process_map.unit_of_work: one security incident or program review

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Prospect and win new accounts
process_map.description: Account executives prospect shippers, visit them to learn their lanes, volumes and freight profile, ask pricing for a proposal and close the account. They work long cycles and compete mainly on price, coverage and service record.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Respond to shipper RFPs
process_map.description: For large shippers' requests for proposal, pricing analysts cost each lane using linehaul and terminal data, the sales manager decides the bid and submits it through the shipper's portal. Bids are due in weeks and award decisions take months.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Price quotes and customer rate agreements
process_map.description: Pricing analysts price spot quotes and account proposals using freight density, lane balance, linehaul cost and competitor rates, then load approved pricing into the rating system as a tariff discount or contract. Pricing errors flow straight into billing errors and disputes.

surge.cause: General rate increase and contract renewal season (shippers re-tender and ask for new quotes after the rate increase notice)

evidence.note: Only 20% to 25% of LTL revenue is subject to the general rate increase, which is applied to the tariff without new quotes, so the season adds less quoting work than the earlier 2 to 4 times; the multiplier is the workflow author's estimate.
Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Renew contracts and apply the general rate increase
process_map.description: Each year sales and pricing review account profitability, negotiate renewals and the general rate increase, and update pricing in the rating system before the effective date. Late updates cause months of rebills.

surge.cause: Annual general rate increase and contract renewal season

evidence.note: Most carriers publish a general rate increase in January and renew many contracts at the start of the year; author's estimate.
Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Set up new customer accounts
process_map.description: The onboarding coordinator creates the customer record with bill-to addresses, billing rules and pricing link, arranges a credit check, and requests EDI or portal set-up. Incomplete set-up sends invoices to the wrong address and delays payment.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Answer shipment trace and status questions
process_map.description: Customer service representatives answer calls and emails asking where freight is, look up scans, ELD positions and delivery receipts, call terminals for missing freight and send proof of delivery. Volume rises sharply when storms or peak delay freight.

surge.cause: Winter storm or highway closure (snowstorms, freezing rain, mountain pass closures)

evidence.note: Storms close Highway 401, the Trans-Canada through the Rockies and the Coquihalla several times each winter; backlog clears over the following days. Author's estimate.
Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Process freight claims
process_map.description: Claims analysts register claims for loss and damage, gather the bill of lading, delivery receipt, OS&D report and invoice, decide carrier liability under the bill of lading terms, and pay, decline or negotiate within authority limits. Slow decisions frustrate customers, and large losses go to insurers.

surge.cause: Autumn shipping peak (September to mid-December retail and industrial restocking)

evidence.note: LTL volumes in Canada rise from September to early December; author's estimate of size.
Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Enter bills of lading as freight bills
process_map.description: Billing clerks key shipper bills of lading from images into the TMS each evening, or check EDI bills, capturing shipper, consignee, pieces, weight, class and special instructions so the freight bill exists before linehaul planning. Handwritten bills, wrong classes and missing consignee details cause errors that surface later as rebills.

surge.cause: Autumn shipping peak (September to mid-December retail and industrial restocking)

evidence.note: LTL volumes in Canada rise from September to early December; author's estimate of size.
Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Rate freight bills and invoice customers
process_map.description: The rating engine prices each freight bill and truckload trip from the customer's agreement, fuel surcharge table and accessorials; billing clerks work the exceptions it cannot rate, and invoices go out daily or on weekly statements by EDI, email or mail. Missing pricing and POD requirements hold invoices.
process_map.unit_of_work: one freight bill rated and invoiced

evidence.note: Fuel surcharge was about 15% of LTL revenue before surcharge at TFI in 2021 and rising at Mullen; process volumes are the author's estimate.

surge.cause: Autumn shipping peak (September to mid-December retail and industrial restocking)

evidence.note: Same autumn peak as bill entry, slightly damped because truckload trips peak less; author's estimate.

process_map.name: Correct bills and resolve billing disputes
process_map.description: Billing auditors process reweigh corrections, accessorial additions and customer disputes, issue rebills or credit notes, and send pricing errors back to pricing. Disputed invoices sit unpaid until resolved.

surge.cause: Annual general rate increase and contract renewal season

evidence.note: Most carriers publish a general rate increase in January and renew many contracts at the start of the year; author's estimate.
Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Collect receivables and apply cash
process_map.description: Collections clerks apply customer payments to invoices, chase overdue accounts, place accounts over their limit on credit hold, and route disputes to billing. Short payments without remittance detail are slow to apply.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Settle owner-operators weekly
process_map.description: Settlements clerks calculate each owner-operator's weekly pay from completed trips at contract rates, add fuel surcharge pass-through, deduct fuel advances, insurance and other chargebacks, and issue the statement and payment. Missing trip paperwork and deduction disputes cause manual adjustments.

evidence.note: Owner-operator and contractor use from Gardewine and Mullen sources; volumes estimated from 380 owner-operators.

process_map.name: Calculate company driver pay
process_map.description: Settlements clerks calculate pay for mileage-paid drivers from trip records and for hourly drivers from timecards, add detention, stop and layover pay, check exceptions against ELD data and send the totals to payroll. Driver pay errors are a common reason drivers quit.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Pay suppliers and carriers
process_map.description: AP clerks match supplier, partner carrier and agent invoices to purchase orders, rate confirmations or settlements, get approvals and pay on terms. Brokered carrier invoices without proof of delivery are held.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Settle interline and partner carrier revenue
process_map.description: Accountants reconcile freight exchanged with interline and US partners each month, agree revenue splits per shipment and pay or bill the net amount. Disagreements over unmatched shipments drag on for months.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: File fuel tax and apportioned registration reports
process_map.description: Accountants compile kilometres by jurisdiction from ELD data and fuel purchases by jurisdiction, prepare the quarterly IFTA return and the IRP renewal, and keep records for audit. Gaps in GPS data lead to estimates and audit risk.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Close the books each month
process_map.description: Finance cuts off postings, accrues unbilled freight, purchased transportation and claims, reconciles accounts and produces monthly results with operating ratio by division for the parent group. Late billing and settlement data delay the close.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Budget and forecast
process_map.description: The planning team builds the annual budget and quarterly forecasts with division leaders, covering volumes, rates, driver headcount, fuel and capital, and agrees them with the parent group. Freight swings in 2020 and 2021 made forecasts unreliable.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Update fuel surcharge tables weekly
process_map.description: Each week a finance analyst takes the published average diesel price, looks up the surcharge percentage in each customer's table and loads it into the rating system and owner-operator settlements. A missed update misprices a whole week of shipments.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Finance equipment
process_map.description: The treasury lead arranges loans and leases for new tractors and trailers within limits set by the parent group, and posts the financing. Rate rises in 2022 raised equipment cost.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Report to the parent group and auditors
process_map.description: The controller prepares quarterly reporting packages for the listed parent and the year-end audit file, and answers auditor questions. Purchase accounting for acquisitions adds work in some years.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Hire dock, shop and office staff
process_map.description: HR coordinators post jobs, screen applicants, arrange interviews with terminal and shop managers, run checks and complete hiring paperwork. Dock turnover is high, and peak season adds casual hiring.

surge.cause: Autumn shipping peak (September to mid-December retail and industrial restocking)

evidence.note: LTL volumes in Canada rise from September to early December; author's estimate of size.
Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Run payroll
process_map.description: Payroll administrators load approved timecards and driver pay records, process new hires, leaves and terminations, run weekly and biweekly payrolls and remit deductions. Several provinces, union rules and mixed pay methods make payroll error-prone.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Manage union relations and grievances
process_map.description: Labour relations managers bargain collective agreements at unionised terminals, answer grievances over discipline, seniority and overtime, and advise managers on contract terms. Grievances that are not settled at the terminal go to arbitration, which takes months.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Manage benefits, leaves and disability
process_map.description: Benefits specialists enrol new employees, process life events, manage short and long-term disability and coordinate return-to-work plans for injured workers with the workers' compensation board.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Run the IT service desk
process_map.description: Service desk technicians fix handheld, ELD, printer and account problems for drivers, dock workers and office staff, replace devices and escalate system faults. ELD malfunctions must be resolved quickly because drivers fall back on paper logs.

evidence.note: ELD malfunction handling from the regulation; ticket volume estimated.

process_map.name: Set up and maintain EDI links
process_map.description: EDI analysts map and test tender, bill of lading, status and invoice messages with customers and partners, and fix failed transmissions. Failed status messages trigger customer complaints and chargebacks.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Change and release systems
process_map.description: Developers and analysts take change requests, configure or code changes in the TMS and other systems, test them with users and release them, and install vendor updates. Changes to rating and billing need careful testing.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Set strategy and pursue acquisitions
process_map.description: The executive team sets the three-year plan within the parent group's targets, decides network expansion and acquisitions of regional carriers, and sets priorities for sales and capital. Acquisition integration is a recurring load on every department.

evidence.note: Growth by acquisition described by Mullen Group (six businesses acquired in 2021); cadence estimated.

process_map.name: Report to the parent group and govern risk
process_map.description: The president and CFO report monthly results, safety performance and risks to the parent group's leadership, and get approval for capital and major contracts. A conditional safety rating, a large claim or a missed budget leads to closer oversight from the parent.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Manage terminal real estate
process_map.description: The facilities manager finds, leases or buys terminal sites, manages expansions, and handles building maintenance and landlord relations. Industrial land shortages in the GTA and Vancouver drove rents up sharply.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Negotiate corporate supply contracts and insurance
process_map.description: Procurement specialists tender and negotiate national contracts for fuel, tires, parts, telecom and services, and run the annual insurance renewal with the broker. Insurance premiums for trucking rose sharply over 2019 to 2022.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Handle legal matters and litigation
process_map.description: Legal staff defend lawsuits from collisions and cargo losses with outside counsel, review customer and supplier contracts, and advise on regulatory matters. Collision lawsuits can run for years and their reserves move the company's results.

evidence.note: Common practice at Canadian LTL and truckload carriers; volumes derived from the demand drivers. Author's estimate.

sources.supports: General rate increases are announced in Q3 or Q4 and take effect in Q1; only about 20% to 25% of LTL carriers' business is subject to them, the rest being under contract or individual pricing.

assumptions: The company is a composite, not a real carrier. Scale and structure are drawn from Mullen Group's LTL segment (including Gardewine) and TFI International's Canadian operations, at about CAD 650 million of revenue in 2021. Headcounts were first set at about 3,000 and revised on 2026-11-24 to 3,603 to cover the work the workflows record; Old Dominion's driver and dock staff per shipment are the outside check.

Employees exclude 380 owner-operators, who are contractors: 310 in truckload (role owner-operator, layer external_party) and 70 who pull LTL linehaul, counted in linehaul-driver as contractor_headcount. Neither group is in the employee count.

Loaded cost = hourly wage x 1.30 for hourly field and dock staff, x 1.35 for salaried office staff (benefits, statutory costs, WSIB/CNESST premiums and overhead). Driver wages come from Job Bank 2024-25 figures for NOC 73300 deflated by about 12% to the 2019-2022 period; other wages are the author's estimates.
US cost benchmarks (ATRI) are converted at about 1.25 CAD per USD and used only to size vehicle running costs; Canadian costs may differ.

Driver turnover is assumed near 15% a year for LTL drivers and near 50% for truckload drivers, below the US figures of 13% and 90% (ATA 2020) for truckload because TFI reports relatively low turnover in Canada.

The ELD mandate took effect in June 2021 with enforcement phased in by provinces afterwards; for 2019 to mid-2021 many drivers used paper logs or unmandated electronic recorders, which made log audits slower.

National Safety Code standards (trip inspection, periodic inspection, facility audit) and Ontario CVOR rules are described from general knowledge; their texts could not be opened, so processes depending on them are tier C.
Process volumes are per month averages over 2019-2022; 2020 volumes fell in the second quarter during COVID-19 lockdowns and 2021-2022 were above average.
Some business units at real carriers are unionised (often Teamsters or Unifor at LTL terminals); this carrier is assumed partly unionised.

Drivers' on-duty hours are nearly all route time, so pickup and delivery drivers are sized at 195 productive hours a month and linehaul drivers at 210 (productive_hours_per_month), not the 130 or 150 the shift-pattern defaults give office and shift staff.
